newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Rockets kill three in Kabul as rebels claim gains.
newsitem.headline: Rockets kill three in Kabul as rebels claim gains.

text.p: Rockets fired at Kabul killed three civilians and wounded nine on Tuesday as Taleban rebels fought to take control of a strategic town east of the city, Kabul radio said.
The government-controlled radio, monitored in Islamabad, said the rockets had been fired by the Taleban into residential areas near Kabul university, whose auditorium was damaged.
Taleban sources in the eastern city of Jalalabad said a government jet had dropped cluster bombs near the city's airport, but had caused no damage or casualties.

The Islamic rebel force has tightened its grip on eastern provinces this month as part of a drive to seize the capital, oust President Burhanuddin Rabbani and impose a strict Islamic order across Afghanistan.

The sources said Taleban fighters trying to capture the strategic town of Sarobi had advanced on two fronts, from Hisarak to Jegdalak mountain, about 10 km (six miles) from Sarobi, and along the main Jalalabad-Kabul highway.
"We are now very close to Sarobi," a Taleban spokesman told the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press news service.

He said eight Taleban fighters had been killed in the latest battles for Sarobi, 70 km (44 miles) east of Kabul. The town controls access to the Tagab Valley leading to the main government airbase at Bagram, 50 km (31 miles) north of Kabul.
Kabul radio said government forces had killed 100 Taleban fighters and had destroyed dozens of military vehicles in the clashes, but did not say if any ground had changed hands.
A Taleban transport plane landed at Bagram on Tuesday, but there were conflicting accounts of the incident.
Kabul radio said the plane carrying 33 Taleban and seven Pakistanis had been hijacked by a "brave mujahid (struggler)" on a flight between the Taleban-held cities of Herat and Kandahar.
Taleban sources confirmed that the plane had landed in Bagram, but said the pilot had defected. They denied any Pakistanis had been on board the aircraft.
The Afghan government accuses Pakistan of supporting the Taleban. Islamabad denies the charge.
A Taleban pilot flew his Mig-21 fighter to Bagram on July 17 and defected to the government.
